headline: Single-cell and spatial omics models probed for specific failure modes
label: Failure Mode Aware Omics Modeling
summary: Recent preprints target named failure modes in single-cell and spatial omics models, from background confounding to outlier, batch, and linear-redundancy…
synthesis: The dominant thread is characterization of where a model fails rather than reliance on an aggregate score. Background-contrastive NMF jointly factorizes target and matched background data with shared non-negative bases to isolate target-enriched topics, directly addressing background confounding. RSTG, a beta-ELBO autoencoder, is evaluated for robustness to outliers, batch effects, and dropouts on MERFISH and MERSCOPE data. PerturbDiff models single-cell perturbation responses as diffusion over distributions embedded in a Hilbert space, capturing hidden-factor variability. The Synergistic Information Score shows that alignment fusion of frozen unimodal encoders captures only linear redundancy. Not every item shares this emphasis, so the common element is target-specific failure characterization rather than a uniform method. What is new is explicit targeting of a named failure mode.
